Package sample.zenoh

Class ZenohJavaTlsSub

java.lang.Object
sample.zenoh.ZenohJavaTlsSub
public class ZenohJavaTlsSub extends Object
mTLS subscriber sample: connects to a Zenoh router over TLS with client certificate authentication, subscribes to a key expression, and prints every unique key it sees (a pragmatic "list topics" for a bus that has no topic registry).

Zenoh, unlike MQTT or Kafka, has no topic list primitive. Keys only exist while something is publishing on them. This sample subscribes to a wildcard key expression, tracks every unique key it observes during the run, and prints a summary on shutdown. Any key that stayed silent during the window will not appear -- that is the best a subscriber can do without a topic-registry service on the router side.

Positional CLI arguments (all optional, in order):

  1. endpoint - Zenoh connect endpoint. Default tls/localhost:7447. Must start with tls/ (or wss/) for this sample; use ZenohJavaSub for plaintext TCP.
  2. rootCaCertPath - path to the CA root PEM used to verify the router's server certificate. Required.
  3. clientCertPath - path to the client leaf certificate PEM (mTLS). Required.
  4. clientKeyPath - path to the client private key PEM (mTLS). Required. PKCS#8 or SEC1 EC (unencrypted).
  5. keyExpr - subscription key expression. Default ** (wildcard: every key on the bus).
  6. timeoutSeconds - optional auto-shutdown timer. Default 0 = run until Ctrl-C.

Hostname verification is disabled in this sample. The typical field usage is connecting to an IP (e.g. a Tailscale / CGNAT 100.x.x.x address) where the router's server cert only lists hostnames as SANs -- the JDK's hostname verifier would reject on IP-to-CN mismatch. Trust is still anchored to the CA root; changing this is a one-line edit in main().
